newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 23.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 23.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The New South Wales government announced on Tuesday it would privatise through a public float its Totalisator Agency Board (TAB), but it said individual stake holders would be limited to five percent each and gaming companies would not be allowed to buy into TAB.

Speculation of a takeover play swirled around the market on Tuesday after about 15 percent of the company's capital was traded in late trade and its share price jumped 20 cents in the last half hour of trade. Newspapers said Japan's Itochu, South Africa's Wooltru and Select and the U.S.-based The Gap were rumoured buyers.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.09 (-0.03)

The leadership of the workers union at Escondida copper mine has recommended to workers that they vote to accept a company pay offer and return to work in a vote Wednesday, a union leader said. The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc.
* Bank of Western Australia Ltd A$2.52 (-0.01)

Bank of Western Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it may not be able to sustain the level of profits achieved in the year to February 28, 1997 due to intense competition, lower lending rates and restructuring costs. Earlier it reported an A$94.5 million profit for the year to end-February compared with its prospectus forecast of a profit of A$100.2 million. The bank warned in February that results were likely to be five percent below the forecast.

Simeon Wines Ltd said on Tuesday it intended to seek a merger with fellow winemaker Australian Vintage Ltd by means of a share and cash offer, valuing Austvin at about A$111 million. Simeon said the offer would be four Simeon shares plus A$3.60 cash for every five Austvin shares. Austvin said early on Wednesday shareholders should not sell their shares ahead of an independent experts report.

Vision Systems Ltd said on Tuesday analysts forecasts for a drop in net profit before abnormals in 1996/97 to about A$7 million were "not too far off the mark", but it expected significant improvements in earnings from new product launches in the next two years.
